rappel_detail.pull: A single 60m rope does every station on this descent; a 70m is not required. Roughly 30m rappels.
rappel_detail.notes: First rappel from the summit ridge, running close to straight down the ridgeline toward Black Tooth Notch.
rappel_detail.anchor: natural/fixed sling on horn or block
hazards: this rappel is the one repeatedly named for pulling rock down onto the person below
a doubled 50m rope will not reach the next station
rappel_detail.station: Reached by downclimbing roughly 100 ft from the summit to the first slings. These are the same anchors you climb past on the final pitches up and right — note where they are on the ascent, because they are much harder to spot on the way down.

rappel_detail.pull: Extending the rings out from the anchor is specifically recommended here to keep the pull clean.
rappel_detail.notes: Second rappel, notably traversing (trending skier's right/rappeller's left).
hazards: the sideways line offers the rope many places to catch and is the station most often named in stuck-rope accounts
enough swing that parties describe hooking a horn on the way across to stop the pendulum
rappel_detail.station: Distinctly traversing, trending skier's right and rappeller's left rather than down the fall line.

rappel_detail.notes: Third rappel, also traversing, reaching Black Tooth Notch; from there scramble/simul-climb an exposed 4th-class connecting ledge.
hazards: the last few feet often need to be scrambled off rappel; setting an intermediate anchor is optional
the connecting ledge to the notch is a short loose Class 4 to low-5th traverse with one exposed move, usually simul-climbed or short-roped
the rope pulls with real drag off the slab at the bottom of this one
rappel_detail.station: The second traversing rappel, ending on or just above the long sidewalk ledge that leads around to Black Tooth Notch. A cairn marks the notch and can be seen on the way up, so note its position before you need it.

rappel_detail.notes: First of three further rappels down into the Southwest Couloir.
hazards: the next station is out of sight from this one; accounts disagree on whether it lies on a hidden ledge to rappeller's left or straight down at the very end of a 60m rope, so be ready for either before you commit
some parties skip this station and scramble about 15 m down to the next
rappel_detail.station: Ten to thirty feet down the southwest side of the notch on fixed slings, at the top of the Southwest Couloir. From here the line runs down the fall line, so you are hunting tat rather than a landmark.

hazards: the rock through the couloir is thoroughly loose and the second person down is directly beneath whatever the first dislodges
a 60m rope is just barely long enough on one of the raps in this section
rappel_detail.station: Straight down the couloir on fixed slings.

rappel_detail.notes: Final rappel into the Southwest Couloir, from which the descent continues toward North Fork Bridge Creek.
hazards: the couloir ends in cliffs and a waterfall band below; exit left onto easier terrain and traverse back into the basin rather than following the fall line, which cliffs out
the exit ledges are crumbly, and there is still several thousand feet of off-trail ground below before the valley — parties get benighted on it
rappel_detail.station: The final rappel takes you off technical rock into the open couloir, landing on Class 3 ground or snow depending on season.

set.rappels: 6 single-rope rappels on a 60 m rope down the Southwest Couloir descent: 3 from the summit to Black Tooth Notch (the second and third traversing), then 3 straight down into the couloir
set.rappel_count_note: Six is the commonly cited/historical rappel count; some parties link stations differently and report as few as five. A single 60m rope suffices for every station.
